value.rationale: Defines a natural inverse problem for epidemic source localization using only aggregate final sizes under unknown common transmissibility, and proves a sharp change in structural identifiability at the smallest nontrivial path order, persisting at arbitrary sizes. A novel low-/high-transmission sign reversal shows why variance may fail to disambiguate equal-mean candidate sources. It distinguishes information in moments from the known-p mean and the full observed size law, making precise what extra data sources would be needed. Its mathematical importance is a structural threshold, not a claim of epidemiological field efficacy.
